intro: The Andante of Haydn’s Symphony No. 94, the “Surprise”, opens with a short C major tune played softly by the strings, followed by a single chord from the full orchestra. The rest of the movement is built on the same tune.

sections.label: Theme · Strings, then a full-orchestra chord
sections.mNote: The tune is repeated and ends on a full-orchestra chord.

sections.label: Var 1 · First violins decorate the theme
sections.mNote: Second violins and violas play the melody underneath

sections.label: Var 2 · C minor, forte
sections.mNote: The violins exchange phrases as the harmony moves through darker keys

sections.label: Var 3 · Oboe, then flute duet
sections.mNote: The melody returns in C major in the winds.

sections.label: Var 4 · Full orchestra, march rhythm
sections.mNote: Full orchestra alternates with strings and bassoon, played quietly

sections.label: Coda · Winds over a held C
sections.mNote: The strings play new chords beneath the theme

cues.title: Opening theme and fortissimo chord
cues.text: The violins play a short theme in C major, and the bass adds a note at the start of each bar. The first phrase is repeated pianissimo, with pizzicato strings. Then the full orchestra plays a fortissimo G major chord.
cues.evidence: Andante, bars 1–16: the string theme, pianissimo pizzicato repeat and G major chord. https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/94._Sinfonie_(Haydn)
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: First variation
cues.text: In the first variation (bars 33–48) the second violins and violas play the theme while the first violins add a semiquaver counterpoint above it. A flute joins some of the answering phrases.
cues.evidence: Andante, first variation, bars 33–48: theme in second violins and violas, with first-violin and flute counterpoint. https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/94._Sinfonie_(Haydn)
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Griesinger’s biography of Haydn, 1810
cues.text: In Griesinger’s 1810 biography, Haydn described his aim in London: “I wanted to surprise the public with something new.” His pupil Pleyel was then writing for a rival concert series. Haydn intended to make the stronger impression.
cues.evidence: Georg August Griesinger, Biographische Notizen über Joseph Haydn (1810), recollection of a conversation with Haydn. Our translation of “das Publikum durch etwas Neues zu überraschen”; German text reproduced at https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/94._Sinfonie_(Haydn)

cues.title: Second variation, C minor
cues.text: The second variation is in C minor. Loud unison phrases alternate with quiet string passages, and the first and second violins then exchange phrases through E♭ major and F minor.
cues.evidence: Andante, second variation, bars 49–74: shortened opening, violin dialogue and E♭ major and F minor passages. https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/94._Sinfonie_(Haydn)
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Third variation, oboe and flute
cues.text: C major returns with the oboe. Later the flute joins it in a duet, and the violins play the melody beneath the two wind instruments.
cues.evidence: Andante, third variation, bars 75–106: oboe opening and the flute–oboe–violin combination. https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/94._Sinfonie_(Haydn)
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Fourth variation, full orchestra
cues.text: The full orchestra plays the fourth variation fortissimo, with off-beat accompaniment. A passage for strings and bassoon follows, marked piano, before the full orchestra returns fortissimo.
cues.evidence: Andante, fourth variation, bars 107–138; quiet strings and bassoon at bars 115–130. https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/94._Sinfonie_(Haydn)
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Coda over a C pedal
cues.text: In the coda, from bar 139, the winds play the theme above held string chords. The harmony moves through seventh and ninth chords over a C pedal in the bass.
cues.evidence: Andante, coda from bar 139: seventh and ninth chords above a C pedal. https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/94._Sinfonie_(Haydn). Wind melody and altered string harmonies: https://www.laphil.com/works/symphony-no-94-surprise
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

transitions.title: First variation adds violin semiquavers
transitions.from: Theme · Strings, then a full-orchestra chord
transitions.to: Var 1 · First violins decorate the theme
transitions.how: The theme closes in C major. An orchestral chord opens the first variation (bars 32–48), in which the second violins and violas take the melody and the first violins play running semiquavers above it. The bass follows the same harmonic progression as in the theme, and the Andante tempo is unchanged.
transitions.evidence: Andante, bars 32–48: first-variation scoring and counterpoint. https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/94._Sinfonie_(Haydn)

transitions.title: C major to C minor
transitions.from: Var 1 · First violins decorate the theme
transitions.how: C major changes to C minor in the second variation, which begins in bar 49. E♭ replaces E♮ above the same home note. The orchestra plays the opening phrase loudly in unison, and quiet strings then play a shortened answer. Haydn joins the beginning of the original tune directly to its ending, which compresses the theme’s two halves.
transitions.evidence: Andante, second variation from bar 49: mode change and compression of the theme’s two halves. https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/94._Sinfonie_(Haydn)

transitions.title: From the minor variation to the third
transitions.how: A falling figure in the first violins leads out of the minor variation. The next statement returns to C major, with the tune in the first oboe above the strings. Later the melody passes to the violins, and flute and oboe add their own parts above it.
transitions.evidence: Andante, end of second variation and third variation, bars 74–106. https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/94._Sinfonie_(Haydn)

transitions.title: Into the fourth variation
transitions.how: The variation led by the winds closes with a cadence in C major. The fourth variation follows in the same key and tempo, fortissimo for the full orchestra, over a syncopated accompaniment. Trumpets and timpani join the strings and winds for the march-like opening of the tune (bars 106–114).
transitions.evidence: Andante, bars 106–114: C major cadence and full-orchestra fourth variation. https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/94._Sinfonie_(Haydn)

transitions.title: Coda over a held C
transitions.to: Coda · Winds over a held C
transitions.how: After the final variation, the coda begins at bar 139. The winds play the tune again, and its outline is unchanged. The strings hold seventh and ninth chords beneath it while C stays in the bass.
transitions.evidence: Andante, coda from bar 139, https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/94._Sinfonie_(Haydn); Orrin Howard’s description of wind melody and string harmonies, https://www.laphil.com/works/symphony-no-94-surprise

source.title: Haydn, Symphony No. 94, full score (Leipzig: Breitkopf & Härtel, ed. Rietz, plate 8876, [1855])
source.locator: Andante, printed pp. 19–29: theme, four variations and coda.

timeline.note: The strings play the quiet tune; its first phrase returns still softer and plucked.
The whole orchestra strikes the fortissimo G major chord.
Flute and oboe join the violin tune; horns hold soft notes beneath them.
The first violins decorate the tune in second violins and violas; flute joins the answering phrases.
The strings continue the first variation on their own.
Winds and strings strike out fortissimo in C minor.
Trumpets and timpani join the C minor climax while the horns rest.
The oboe brings back C major above bassoons and semiquavers in the violins.
Flute and oboe play a duet above the tune in the violins.
Soft held horn notes support the flute and oboe.
The fourth variation starts fortissimo, with brass, timpani and running violin scales.
Strings and bassoons answer the loud orchestra, piano dolce.
Tremolo strings lead the crescendo to a fortissimo chord held under a fermata.
The winds play the tune again above held string chords and a C in the bass.

quote.text: The whole company was extremely pleased, and so was I.
quote.source: London notebook, after his benefit concert on 4 May 1795; our translation

composer.background:
On 4 May 1795, Haydn gave a benefit concert at the King’s Theatre in London. The programme included his new D major Symphony, now numbered 104. Afterwards he wrote in his notebook: “The whole company was extremely pleased, and so was I. I made four thousand gulden this evening. Such a thing can only be done in England.” He was sixty-three. He was a wheelwright’s son and had spent most of his adult life in the livery of a servant of the Esterházy family.

Haydn was born in Rohrau in 1732. His father was a wheelwright who played the harp by ear and sang; his mother had worked as a cook. At about six, Joseph left home for schooling in Hainburg. By 1740 he was a choirboy at St Stephen’s Cathedral in Vienna. As a chorister he sang church music daily but received little instruction in composition. Performances outside the cathedral also gave him chances to get a meal. When his voice broke and he was dismissed in 1749, another musician, Johann Michael Spangler, took him into his family’s crowded room.
